chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Umar ibn Yazeed, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:
Do not accompany the people of innovation, and do not sit with them, lest you become in the eyes of the people like one of them.
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'A person is upon the religion of his close friend and companion.'

key_terms.أَهْلَ الْبِدَعِ: People of innovation (those who introduce religious deviations)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on sitting with people of religious innovation in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) warns against socializing with Ahl al-Bid'ah to preserve communal identity and prevent the erosion of religious distinction, emphasizing that proximity leads to perceived association. This concept of 'Qaraba' (companionship) influencing one's spiritual state is rooted in the Prophetic maxim that a person follows the faith of their close friend, a principle widely cited in Shia jurisprudence to justify selective social engagement. The warning serves as a practical guideline for maintaining doctrinal purity in mixed religious environments.
